native_result.query: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, how does the number of monuments and axes changes with elements of symbolic capital?
native_result.HypoA: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, the number of monuments and axes increases along with symbolic capital
native_result.HypoB: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE monuments and axes increase together while elements of symbolic capital do not: MonumentCount rises +0.10 Z (-0.47 -> -0.36, peaking at +0.91 in 3200 BCE) and AxesCelts +0.43 Z (+0.37 -> +0.80, peaking at +2.60 in 3200 BCE), the two tracking each other (descriptive r = 0.87), whereas Hatchets&Swords stay pinned at the floor of their record (~-0.43 Z, dZ 0.00), Daggers are constant at their record minimum (-0.58 Z, zero variance) and House Size falls steeply (dZ -1.86, ~-0.46 Z/century) from the highest value in the whole dataset (2.05 Z) to near average. We therefore hypothesise that monumental construction and axe deposition after 3400 BCE were driven by a communal/dedicatory dynamic decoupled from prestige-goods and household symbolic display: monuments and axes peaked around 3200 BCE precisely while house size, daggers and hatchets/swords were static or contracting, associations are uniformly weak (all |r| <= 0.36, CIs about -0.95..+0.93; bin-to-bin sign agreement with House Size 1/3 for monuments, 2/2 for axes), and the post-3200 BCE decline of monuments and axes cannot be attributed to symbolic capital, which never varied in this window. Caveats: House Size is also an economic/domestic proxy; all statistics rest on 5 independent 100-year bins so direction, magnitude and rank order carry the argument; magnitudes are Z-standardised because the data contain no absolute counts.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parse capital.csv with comma->decimal conversion, convert BCE to signed CE (CE = -BCE); verified identical (max abs diff 0.0) to time_series_data.csv raw Z columns, so it is used as the canonical 100-year raw-Z table. 2) Slice 3400-3000 BCE inclusive = 5 bins (all period MN). 3) Per series report levels, dZ 3400->3000, OLS slope per century with stderr, direction class (|dZ|<0.1 flat), up/down steps, unique counts, and rank order of change. 4) Descriptive Pearson r with Fisher-z 95% CI plus Spearman rho for MonumentCount/AxesCelts vs each symbolic element, printing the |r| needed for p<0.05 at n=5; Dagger skipped (zero variance) and described by levels. 5) PRIMARY co-movement evidence: bin-to-bin change-sign agreement, corr of changes, rank order of total change, plus focal-focal (MonumentCount vs AxesCelts) and non-symbolic context series. 6) Pollen openness sidebar from Belau-only pollen_inter / pollen_inter_100 (annual, interpolated) with two-site MEAN/SMOOTH_MEAN_100y shown as an option; flagged exploratory and excluded from the hypothesis. 7) Labelled robustness: 3500-2800 BCE (n=8), all-MN (equals the window), and annual-interpolated slopes reported as descriptive only to avoid pseudo-replication. 8) Tables exported to out/results.xlsx and CSVs; full stdout in out/analysis_output.txt.
